claims.summary: Over F2[z,a,b,c] with independent variables, set B=z(z+1), s=a+b+c, P0=z(z+a)(z+b)(z+c), P1=P0(z+1), P2=(a+1)(b+1)(c+1). For every M=2^t,t>=0, the three affine products Qi=Pi^M are pairwise coprime and none of their pair sums is a product of binary affine polynomials, while their full sum is B^M s^M. Its exact root order at both0,1 is M and its quotient s^M has depth at most two and size O(M+1) with ordinary power wires. Leading and constant coefficients rule out splitting of the base pair sums; translation handles the last pair and UFD preserves nonsplitting under powers. For any unit-generating binary input tuple F containing B with these distinct old variables, supply H=(s sum_(i!=B)Fi Zi)^M+Z_B^M sum_i Pi^M. It equals s^M(F dot Z)^M and is invariant on every full coefficient certificate. Its reciprocal numerator construction produces the literal triple after pruning the zero branch. Inputs of joint size u, depth delta_F and r labels give probe size O(u+r+M+1) and constant added depth. Polynomial M in a Boolean-unsatisfiable CNF encoding N gives unbounded polynomial-size source-admissible witnesses without a small certificate assumption. This refutes a mandatory affine-pair-merger step, not general division: complete factorization and global Frobenius deflation give cheap alternatives. Combined-move or arbitrary triple coverage and the Frege lower bound remain open.
